note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Cost of the Fisher diagonal motivates recycling the Adam accumulator as the Squisher, validated empirically

nodes.name: Fisher diagonal measures parameter sensitivity
nodes.description: The Fisher diagonal is widely used as a measure of parameter sensitivity in applications such as pruning, sparse training, continual learning, task similarity and model merging.

nodes.name: Computing the Fisher is costly and inconvenient
nodes.description: Computing the Fisher diagonal requires per-example gradients on sampled labels, often done with a batch size of one, and needs training data that may be unavailable; this hinders adoption, e.g. Fisher Merging is absent from mergekit.

nodes.name: Adaptive optimizers keep squared-gradient accumulators
nodes.description: Adam-style optimizers maintain an exponential moving average of squared gradients, available for free at the end of training.

nodes.name: Joint Fisher is a square of sums
nodes.description: The joint (empirical) Fisher is a square of aggregated gradients rather than a sum of squares, which gives theoretical motivation for relating the squared-gradient accumulator to the Fisher diagonal; joint and standard Fisher coincide (Lin et al. 2024).

nodes.name: Accumulator differs from Fisher in EMA and bias
nodes.description: The accumulator averages over a long EMA history (time constant about 10,000 steps for beta2 = 0.999), including gradients at old parameters, so it is a biased estimate of the joint empirical Fisher and needs rescaling when magnitudes matter.

nodes.name: Squisher is the accumulator used as Fisher
nodes.description: The Squisher uses the squared gradient accumulator in place of the Fisher diagonal, directly where only relative parameter importance matters and with a rescaling term where magnitudes matter.

nodes.name: Squisher matches Fisher across settings
nodes.description: Across six settings spanning five applications, replacing the Fisher with the Squisher had little impact on performance and consistently outperformed Fisher-free baselines.

nodes.name: Squisher costs nearly nothing
nodes.description: Computing the Squisher takes under 0.1 seconds in all settings (under 1 second for EWC), versus substantial time to compute the Fisher.

nodes.name: Rescaling matters in continual learning
nodes.description: In continual learning, using the squared gradient accumulator without tuning the rescaling term lambda gives suboptimal results.

nodes.name: Unfinished training hurts the Squisher
nodes.description: Squisher performance can degrade when fine-tuned models are not fully trained, since the accumulator has seen too few steps; beta2 = 0.95 degrades performance while the default 0.999 is best.

nodes.name: Explicit joint Fisher is close to Fisher
nodes.description: Explicitly squaring the sum of per-example gradients (turning off the moving average) gives results close to the Fisher, suggesting the joint Fisher is a useful approximation.

isolated_nodes.name: Fisher is not trivially the accumulator
isolated_nodes.description: Despite Adam's paper asserting the accumulator approximates the Fisher diagonal without evidence, the two differ in subtle ways that require modifications to use the accumulator successfully.

isolated_nodes.name: Fisher merging is rescaling-invariant
isolated_nodes.description: Fisher Merging is invariant to rescaling all Fisher values by a constant, so using the Squisher or the raw accumulator as Fisher proxies yields the same merge.

isolated_nodes.name: Differences are noise-level
isolated_nodes.description: Performance differences between Fisher and Squisher are problem-dependent and small relative to baselines, largely attributable to noise, so neither is claimed superior.

isolated_nodes.name: Pruning marginally degrades, merging improves
isolated_nodes.description: With the Squisher, performance degraded marginally in Fisher pruning, improved in Fisher merging, and was almost identical in other settings.

isolated_nodes.name: Per-sample gradient libraries are limited
isolated_nodes.description: Specialized per-sample gradient libraries add overhead, require code changes and lack full architecture support (e.g. layer normalization), unlike the Squisher.

isolated_nodes.name: Unbiasedness requires model-sampled labels
isolated_nodes.description: Mini-batch Fisher estimation is unbiased only when labels are sampled from the model's likelihood; with empirical labels the estimators are biased.

structural_reasoning: Cost motivation and the square-of-sums argument lead to the Squisher definition, whose validity is shown by performance, runtime and ablation results.
